before: A new room seeded no paragraph identity for notes, so a received note edit differed from the author until the receiver opened its notes store. Tombstoned node records counted against the 200,000 node cap, so long-lived rooms ended at that total. Hosts could only poll room size.
after: A new room seeds notes paragraph identity, so both peers agree before either opens the notes store. Live node records count against the 200,000 node cap and every record counts against a 400,000 record ceiling. Sessions push a notification when a room crosses a fraction of any cap.
reason: Shared records, text offsets, operations, and repair rules keep their meaning. Seeded paraIds are ordinary attributes released readers already store and serialize, and rooms seeded before this change behave as before. The node caps are a local, fail-closed refusal that writes nothing to shared state: replicas of this release decide identically on the same state, and a released replica that meets a room over 200,000 records stops with the same terminal too-many-nodes it reports today, without diverging content. The blob cap and the pressure signal do not change accepted state.
